### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []` in the dev report — none to answer. Seven declared deviations and two out-of-scope findings, each judged:

1. **`.claude/agents/os-dev.md` says `pr_create` carries `assignees: [LOGIN]`; the order forbade it.** Process, not this tree; the PR correctly carries no assignee under the maintainer's 2026-10-29 ruling on #27363. 2. **Partial rebuild (spec + client-react closure, not full `pnpm build`); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally.** Answered by the head's check-runs: Build Core, Test Core, TypeScript Type Check and Lint & Repo Gates all `success`. Closed.

Payable text under the ruling's "deleted word / removed duplicate" reading. Accepted.
4. **`skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md` not updated (ceiling 143, headroom 1).** Harmless; the README is an index, the new case is discoverable by id. Accepted.
5. **Pre-existing `must_not_contain` self-contradictions in `skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json` evals 1/2/4/7 left as written.** Verified on `origin/main` byte-for-byte (the same six strings: `tableName`; `data:beforeInsert`, `onInstall`; `@objectstack/adapter-`; `role:`, `admin_full_access`) — not introduced here, and the new eval 9 is clean. Should-fix outside this PR; escalated: the `domain:skills` seat files the card the dev named ("noted, not filed") — it is the defect class changeset `26515-automation-eval-fixtures.md` already repaired for the automation skill.
6. **No frontmatter edit, so the automation `description` does not name assignment rules.** Accepted for this PR (the regenerated `skills-reference.mdx` is another lane's file). Should-fix follow-up: a one-line `description` addition so the family is routed by the skill picker, coordinated with the docs lane.
7. **`test:repo` not run locally.** Test Core `success` on the head. Closed.

Out-of-scope finding 2 (PM fold-home hypothesis partly falsified) is reporting, not a defect; no action.

### ④ Design judgment

Each `hits` file read against the card's prompt ("teach ownership queues and assignment rules … with eval prompts; the `queue` approver type"), ADR-0142 D1–D7 and the spec/runtime on the head.

**`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` — § Ownership queues.** Holds. "Every `ownership: 'user'` object carries a platform-injected `queue` column beside `owner_id`" — `injected-system-columns.ts` L240–252 (`queue = owner`). "An object declaring its own `queue` field is refused" — `registry.ts#objectQueueColumnRefusal` (422 `ObjectQueueColumnRefusedError`, prescription: rename or leave the `user` tier). "Sits in a queue when `owner_id` is empty and `queue` names it: members read and edit it (rows widen, verbs never — no delete)" — ADR-0142 D3 verbatim semantics (disjunct in `buildReadFilter`/update arm/`checkEdit`, never the delete paths). "Declared members are positions only; an organization adds users and teams through `sys_queue_member`" — `DeclaredQueueMemberSchema` refusal text. The `defineQueue` example parses (`name` snake_case, `label`, `members[]`) and is type-checked by `check:skill-examples` (Lint & Repo Gates green; the PR's reverse leg shows the block is live). Claim as a by-id `{ owner_id: <self> }` update admitted to a member on an unowned record, loser `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE` — D4 + `ownership-queue-gate.ts#CLAIM_REFUSAL` + `concurrent-update-error.ts` ("The record was taken"). Release = owner writes `owner_id: null`, record sits in its home queue again — D4 + `RELEASE_REFUSAL`. Move = writing another `queue` is a transfer (`allowTransfer` or `modifyAllRecords`) — D3/D4 + `MOVE_REFUSAL`. The refused alternatives (`assigned_to` picklist, counter field, owner-picking hook) are exactly ADR-0142 D8's STOPGAP list. Folds verified at their homes: `rules/naming.md` L7–13 (table), `rules/field-types.md` L9 ("49 available"), L44–45 (`password`/`secret`), L98 (`user`), L110–118 (embedded), `rules/indexing.md` L26–33 (retired `type`/`partial`), L40–80 (unique scope, bare `true`, FIELD rule). No fact lost. **No finding.**

**`skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`.** Holds. `current_user.queues` row cites ADR-0142 D3 and `rls.zod.ts` names `queues` kernel-resolved — right; `plugin-security/src/kernel-queue-membership.ts` is the producer. The `sharedWith: { type: 'queue', value }` sentence ("shares the rule's rows, parks none — only the record's `queue` column does that") is ADR-0142 D7's closing sentence and matches `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx` L189. Tightened paragraphs (permissionSets refusal, Layer-0 blockquote, viewAllRecords, `secret`, renaming) keep every fact. **Should-fix (wording, not blocking):** the placeholder row reads "the ownership queues the caller *sits in*" — the skill's own § Ownership queues defines *sits in* for records; a caller *is a member of* a queue. One word (`belongs to`), zero token cost.

**`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` — § Assignment rules.** Holds. "Routes each inserted row of an `ownership: 'user'` object whose `owner_id` and `queue` are both still empty — once, after every `beforeInsert` hook, never on update, never refusing the insert (ADR-0142 D5)" — `AssignmentRuleSchema` TSDoc and D5 word for word. "Entries ordered; the first whose `criteria` (CEL over `record.*`) match decides" — `AssignmentRuleEntrySchema`; a bare string is CEL shorthand (`EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` L269–272), so `criteria: 'record.priority == "urgent"'` and `load: 'record.status != "closed"'` are valid input. The example's two entries exercise both arms the refinements allow: queue target without strategy (parks) and `least_loaded` with `load`; the comment "`load` only with least_loaded" is the refinement's own rule. "`strategy` is for a queue target only" — refinement 1. The `queue` approver pointer resolves: `references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` L236 `### Approver Types`, L247 the `queue` row ("at node entry; an empty queue adds nobody") — `approval-service.ts` L2473/L2522–2532 implements exactly that. Folds: item 5 → `requires` table L343 (`messaging` … `skipped: true`); item 4's stdlib/brace rule kept in the surviving item 4; item 3's dispatch sentence kept in the node table L89 and the rewritten item 3; When-to-Use bullets → one paragraph that now names the family; Blueprint table → one paragraph with the same four facts. **Should-fix (prose, not blocking):** "The third automation family" has no antecedent in the file (When to Use names six things); "Another automation family" or dropping the ordinal reads cleaner. **No must-fix.**

**`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` — the `queues`/`assignmentRules` paragraph.** Holds against the code: the boot refusal is `objectql/src/plugin.ts#assertOwnershipQueueServicePresent` at `kernel:ready` → `describeMissingOwnershipQueueService` (probes the `ownership-queue` service, "never the job queue's `queue`"), and `plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts` L707 registers it. The paragraph sits after the key enumeration, outside what `check-skill-top-level-keys` parses (green). Folds verified: `references/operations.md` L61 `## Ports & networking` (anchor `#ports--networking`), `references/bootstrap.md` L100 `### Programmatic Bootstrap (Without CLI)` (anchor `#programmatic-bootstrap-without-cli`), `objectstack-data/references/seeds.md` L59 `### Import modes` with the five-mode table (anchor `#import-modes`). **Should-fix (precision, not blocking):** "(`sharing` in `requires`): a stack declaring either without it is refused at boot" lets "it" read as the token. `sharing` is on `PLATFORM_ALWAYS_ON_CAPABILITIES` (`platform-capabilities.ts` L357), so under default `os serve` the service is mounted whether or not `requires` names it; the refusal fires where the SERVICE is absent (`--preset minimal`, a programmatic boot without `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`). Declaring `sharing` is still right under the skill's own "Declaring is a demand" rule (an absent provider becomes a hard error instead of best-effort), so nothing an AI writes from this sentence is refused or silently wrong — hence should-fix: say "the service `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` registers — demand it with `sharing` in `requires`; a composition without it is refused at boot".

**`skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json` — eval 8.** Holds. The model answer's `defineQueue({ name: 'inside_sales', label, members: [{ type: 'position', value: 'inside_sales_rep' }] })` parses; a queue-target entry with no `strategy` parks (D5); the claim and `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE` are D4. `expected_output` contains all four `must_contain` strings and neither `must_not_contain` string (checked). The prompt ("two reps must never own the same lead") is answered by the one-owner precondition. Evals 1–7 keep every `must_contain` token. **No finding.**

**`skills/objectstack-automation/evals/flows-triggers-approvals.json` — eval 12.** Holds. `defineAssignmentRule({ … entries: [{ name: 'all', assignTo: { type: 'queue', value: 'support_team' }, strategy: 'round_robin' }] })` passes every refinement (`round_robin` takes no `load`); "evaluated once per insert on a still-ownerless row, never on update" is D5; the `queue` approver sentence is D6 and the `ApproverType` comment. This is the first eval exercising the `queue` approver type the card asked for. All four `must_contain` present, neither `must_not_contain` present. Evals 1–11 keep every token. **No finding.**

**`skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json` — eval 9.** Holds. Two collections, `'sharing'` in `requires`, "`queue` is the job queue" (the contract header's own distinction). Self-consistent. The pre-existing contradictions in evals 1/2/4/7 are on `main` unchanged and carried in ③ item 5. **No finding on the new case.**

Nothing in the seven `hits` files contradicts the spec, the ADR, the runtime or `content/docs/automation/queues-and-assignment-rules.mdx` on `main`; the three new `os:check`/model-answer shapes are the shapes the schemas accept. Three should-fixes, no must-fix.
